content: 1. Methscopolamine is administered orally at a dose of 5 mg four times daily. The initial dose may be increased to 20 mg/day, but it should not exceed 30 mg/day. 2. Co-administration of glucagon and methscopolamine increases the risk of gastrointestinal toxicity due to additive inhibition of gastrointestinal motility. This interaction is mediated by pharmacodynamic mechanisms. Avoid this combination or consider alternative therapies. 3. Intranasal glucagon also increases the toxicity of methscopolamine through similar mechanisms. Avoid concurrent use or substitute with an alternative drug. 4. Topical glycopyrronium tosylate and methscopolamine exhibit pharmacodynamic synergism, leading to additive anticholinergic adverse effects. Avoid this combination or use alternative medications. 5. Pramlintide and methscopolamine both inhibit gastrointestinal motility through synergistic pharmacodynamic effects. This combination is contraindicated due to the risk of severe gastrointestinal complications. 6. Co-administration of revefenacin and methscopolamine results in additive anticholinergic effects due to decreased cholinergic transmission. Avoid this combination or use alternative therapies. 7. Methscopolamine reduces the efficacy of secretin by pharmacodynamic antagonism. This interaction may impair the response to stimulation testing with secretin. Discontinue anticholinergic drugs at least five half-lives before administering secretin. 8. Topical sofpironium and methscopolamine exhibit additive anticholinergic adverse effects due to pharmacodynamic synergism. Avoid this combination or use alternative therapies. 9. Methscopolamine and inhaled umeclidinium bromide/vilanterol increase each other's toxicity through pharmacodynamic synergism. Avoid concurrent use or consider alternative treatments. 10. Methscopolamine enhances the effects of abobotulinumtoxinA through pharmacodynamic synergism. Use caution and monitor for excessive neuromuscular weakness and heightened systemic anticholinergic effects. 11. Methscopolamine and aclidinium both decrease cholinergic transmission, leading to additive anticholinergic effects. Use caution and monitor for adverse effects. 12. Aluminum hydroxide reduces the absorption of methscopolamine by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor for reduced therapeutic efficacy. 13. Methscopolamine and amantadine exhibit pharmacodynamic synergism, increasing the risk of anticholinergic adverse effects. Use caution and monitor for signs of toxicity. 14. Methscopolamine and amitriptyline both decrease cholinergic transmission, resulting in additive anticholinergic effects. Use caution and monitor for adverse reactions. 15. Methscopolamine and amoxapine also decrease cholinergic transmission, leading to additive anticholinergic effects. Use caution and monitor for potential side effects. 16. Methscopolamine reduces the absorption of aripiprazole by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both drugs. Additionally, aripiprazole increases the effects of methscopolamine through pharmacodynamic synergism. Use caution and monitor for additive anticholinergic effects and potential hypoglycemia. 17. Atracurium and methscopolamine both decrease cholinergic transmission, leading to additive anticholinergic effects. Use caution and monitor for adverse reactions. 18. Atropine and methscopolamine exhibit additive anticholinergic effects due to decreased cholinergic transmission. Use caution and monitor for potential side effects. 19. Belladonna alkaloids and methscopolamine both decrease cholinergic transmission, resulting in additive anticholinergic effects. Use caution and monitor for adverse reactions. 20. Methscopolamine reduces the absorption of benperidol by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Additionally, benperidol increases the effects of methscopolamine through pharmacodynamic synergism. Use caution and monitor for additive anticholinergic effects and potential hypoglycemia. 21. Methscopolamine and benztropine both decrease cholinergic transmission, leading to additive anticholinergic effects. Use caution and monitor for adverse reactions. 22. Bethanechol increases cholinergic transmission, while methscopolamine decreases it. The net effect of this interaction is unclear. Use caution and monitor for unexpected outcomes. 23. Buprenorphine (long-acting injection) enhances the effects of methscopolamine through pharmacodynamic synergism. Co-administration may increase the risk of urinary retention and/or severe constipation, potentially leading to paralytic ileus. Use caution and monitor for these complications. 24. Calcium carbonate reduces the absorption of methscopolamine by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor for reduced therapeutic efficacy. 25. Carbachol increases cholinergic transmission, while methscopolamine decreases it. The net effect of this interaction is unclear. Use caution and monitor for unexpected outcomes.
